nordvpn.tagline: The best all-rounder for most people
nordvpn.verdict: NordVPN combines repeatedly audited no-logs claims, RAM-only servers and the fast NordLynx (WireGuard-based) protocol with a very large network. It is not the cheapest option on a monthly plan, but on long plans it offers the strongest overall package in our scorecard.
pros: No-logs policy audited by Deloitte several times
NordLynx (WireGuard-based) protocol is built for speed
Threat Protection blocks trackers and malicious sites
cons: Renewal prices are higher than the introductory price

expressvpn.tagline: Premium, polished and very easy to use
expressvpn.verdict: ExpressVPN is one of the most polished VPNs available, with RAM-only TrustedServer technology, its own Lightway protocol and excellent router support. It usually costs more than rivals, so it suits people who value simplicity over price.
pros: Lightway protocol is fast and open source
cons: Device limit depends on the plan

surfshark.tagline: Unlimited devices at a budget price
surfshark.verdict: Surfshark lets you connect an unlimited number of devices on one account and is consistently one of the cheapest premium VPNs on long plans. It uses RAM-only servers and had its no-logs policy audited, making it a strong value choice for families and households.
pros: Very low price on long plans
cons: Headquartered in the Netherlands (14 Eyes member)
Renewal price is much higher than the first term

cyberghost.tagline: Beginner-friendly with a generous refund window
cyberghost.verdict: CyberGhost is designed for people who want to install a VPN and forget about it. Its apps are simple, it labels servers by use case and it offers a 45-day money-back window on long plans, although advanced users may find it less configurable.
cons: Owned by Kape, which also owns several other VPNs

protonvpn.tagline: Swiss privacy with the best free plan
protonvpn.verdict: Proton VPN is run by the Swiss company behind Proton Mail. Its apps are open source, its no-logs policy has been independently audited and its free plan has no data cap, which makes it the free VPN we are most comfortable recommending.
pros: Free plan with no data limit
cons: Paid plans cost more than budget rivals
Free plan has limited server locations
Fewer servers than the largest networks

pia.verdict: Private Internet Access offers open-source apps, unlimited devices and deep configuration options at a low long-term price. Its no-logs claims have been tested in real court cases and audited, but its US headquarters is a drawback for some privacy-focused users.
pros: No-logs claims audited and tested in court
cons: Headquartered in the United States (Five Eyes)

ipvanish.verdict: IPVanish owns much of its server infrastructure and allows unlimited devices. It is a reasonable budget choice, but it has a smaller country list than the leaders and is based in the United States.
pros: Owns much of its server network
Scramble option helps on restrictive networks
cons: Headquartered in the United States (Five Eyes)

mullvad.verdict: Mullvad is the privacy purist's VPN: no email address is needed, you can pay with cash, and every plan costs the same flat monthly fee. It runs RAM-only servers and has been audited, but it deliberately does not market itself for streaming.
pros: Account without email or personal data
cons: No affiliate program, so we earn nothing from it

purevpn.verdict: PureVPN has invested in audits and certifications in recent years and is often among the cheapest options on multi-year plans. Its apps and speeds are solid but not class-leading.
cons: Apps feel less polished than the leaders

torguard.tagline: A power-user VPN with dedicated IPs
torguard.verdict: TorGuard is aimed at technical users who want fine control over protocols, ports and dedicated IPs. It is less beginner-friendly and lacks a published independent no-logs audit.
cons: Headquartered in the United States (Five Eyes)

hideme.tagline: Privacy-first with a usable free plan
hideme.verdict: hide.me is a Malaysia-based provider with an audited no-logs policy and a free plan that is safe to use for light browsing. Paid plans are competitive, although its network is smaller than the market leaders.
pros: Based in Malaysia, outside the 14 Eyes
cons: Free plan has a data cap and few locations

astrill.verdict: Astrill offers proprietary protocols and dedicated IPs, but it is expensive, has a small network and has not published an independent no-logs audit. Most people will get more value from the top of our ranking.

fastestvpn.verdict: FastestVPN is one of the cheapest VPNs you can buy and allows many devices, but its network is small and it has not published an independent security audit.
pros: Very low price on long plans

tunnelbear.tagline: The friendliest VPN to start with
tunnelbear.verdict: TunnelBear is the easiest VPN to understand, publishes yearly security audits and offers a small free plan. It is not built for power users, P2P or streaming.
pros: Free plan to try it out
cons: Free plan has a small data cap

hotspotshield.tagline: Fast proprietary protocol and a free tier
hotspotshield.verdict: Hotspot Shield's proprietary Hydra (Catapult) protocol performs well and its free tier is easy to start with. However, the free version shows ads and the company has not published an independent no-logs audit.
cons: Headquartered in the United States (Five Eyes)
Free version shows ads and is limited

fsecure.tagline: Simple VPN from a security company
fsecure.verdict: F-Secure's VPN is a simple, trustworthy add-on from a long-standing Finnish security company. It is fine for basic protection on public Wi-Fi, but its network and feature set are small.
pros: From an established Finnish security company

privatevpn.verdict: PrivateVPN is a small Swedish provider with a simple app, a decent country list and low long-term pricing. It lacks an independent audit and has a small server count.
pros: Around 60 countries despite a small network

ivacy.verdict: Ivacy is among the cheapest VPNs on multi-year plans and covers many countries. It is fine for casual use, but it has not published an independent audit and locks you into long terms for the best price.
pros: Very low price on multi-year plans
cons: Best prices require very long commitments

vyprvpn.tagline: Swiss VPN with its own infrastructure
vyprvpn.verdict: VyprVPN owns and operates its own network and is based in Switzerland. Its Chameleon protocol is helpful on restrictive networks, but it has a small device limit and fewer servers than leaders.
pros: Owns and operates its server network

cactusvpn.verdict: CactusVPN is a small provider with simple apps and flexible short plans. Its network is tiny and it has not published an independent audit, so it ranks near the bottom of our scorecard.
pros: Based in Moldova, outside the 14 Eyes

avast.tagline: Basic VPN from a mass-market antivirus brand
avast.verdict: Avast's VPN is easy to use and comes from a well-known antivirus brand, but VPN is not its core product and Avast has faced past privacy criticism over data practices in other products.
cons: Past privacy controversies at the parent company
